claims.text: The selected HEA contains five or more transition metals in near-equiatomic proportions.
The selected HEA is a single-phase solid solution.
The selected HEA has a random atomic distribution.
The emergence of superconductivity is governed primarily by electronic disorder and the density of states at the Fermi level.
A sufficiently high density of states at the Fermi level permits conventional electron-phonon-mediated pairing despite atomic-scale disorder.
Random atomic distributions and local lattice distortions influence electronic disorder.
Random atomic distributions and local lattice distortions influence the phonon spectrum.
If disorder does not reduce the Fermi-level density of states below the level needed for electron-phonon coupling, Cooper pairs can form and superconductivity can emerge.
An insufficient density of states at the Fermi level inhibits superconductivity.
The HEA is expected to undergo a sharp resistivity drop to zero below a critical temperature.
Disorder may make the HEA's critical temperature lower than those of its pure constituent metals.
The proposed mechanism applies to HEAs containing transition metals that support superconductivity in pure or binary forms.

contradictions.description: The baseline says that no superconducting transition is observed, while the predicted outcome says the same HEA will exhibit a superconducting transition. Restricting the baseline explicitly to room temperature or to T > Tc would remove the ambiguity.
